title: Nyx: Virtualizing dataflow execution on shared FPGA platforms
problem: Existing multi-tenant FPGA virtualization systems support only task-parallel models, where distinct reconfigurable regions process independent data batches — this precludes dataflow execution (direct streaming between pipelined tasks), forcing dependent tasks to wait and incurring long end-to-end response times. No prior work supports dataflow pipelines in a virtualized, shared FPGA environment.
motivation: FPGAs are increasingly deployed as cloud accelerators, and their natural pipelined dataflow execution model is a key performance advantage that is lost when shared across tenants using task-parallel virtualization, creating a gap between FPGA potential and realized multi-tenant efficiency.
method: Nyx divides the FPGA into reconfigurable regions and adds virtual FIFOs (data buffers between tasks) that let dependent tasks exchange data without running simultaneously. The system's controller tracks the queue state and schedules tasks across regions with high throughput, allowing different pipelines to share the same hardware by running at different times.
key_novelty: Virtual FIFOs enable pipelined tasks to stream data between each other and run at different times on shared FPGA regions instead of requiring all pipeline stages to run simultaneously.
contributions: First system to enable dataflow execution in a virtualized, multi-tenant shared FPGA environment
Virtual FIFO abstraction that decouples pipelined tasks from their communication partners across scheduling epochs
FPGA hypervisor design that tracks data dependencies and dispatches pipelined tasks efficiently across reconfigurable regions
Empirical evaluation showing 1.26x-8.87x throughput improvement and 2.8x-3.28x response-time reduction over task-parallel virtualization baselines

metrics.speedup: 1.26x-8.87x throughput over state-of-the-art task-parallel virtualized FPGA; 2.8x-3.28x response time reduction in low-demand periods; 2x-2.75x in high-demand periods
metrics.other: deadline violations reduced by up to 76.5% (low demand), 34.5% (high demand); tail response time reduced up to 1.9x

limitations: Evaluation scope and overhead of virtual FIFO management (memory, routing resources) are not discussed in the abstract.
